texts: good. "took place" keeps the date on the equinox itself — past tense plus both the day and the year — so nothing in the sentence is lost. One caveat for the corpus as a whole: day 0 lands in the ordinary calendar day-of-month slot, which has no epoch-day reading behind it, so day numbers on their own will not put events in order; the relative wordings you use elsewhere ("two days before the autumn equinox") are what actually carry the sequence.

good. parses as a fireable rule — every autumn equinox gets its own beginning event, with the equinox as the one doing the beginning and moth-season as what begins — and the word "every" is recorded alongside it.
good. "East Row" is taken as a name, the lantern-row kind carries its "row" genus, and "on the Cliff Path" is kept as a position of the row itself rather than folded into a containment claim.
good. same shape as the East Row sentence, and the Cliff Path is the same symbol introduced there, so both rows are attached to one path.
good. the harbor wall gets its own referent with its "wall" genus, and "along" is kept as the stated relation between the row and the wall.

good. the name, the lantern-station kind with its "station" genus, and both position relations are all there; note that "near the harbor" was read as describing the Harbor Station rather than the Cliff Path.
